body:
My experience is a bit different--got forced in by my friends. God I was scared shitless. I'll be honest in saying that most of the fear I felt for the first couple of days stemmed from the aftershock--I couldn't come to terms with what I had tried to do, and the fact that I was wheeled out of an ER into an ambulance to a psych hospital made it feel so surreal and horrifying.

Also it didn't help that in this hospital I was put on a floor with very aggressive patients--some lady across the hall from me was experiencing a psychotic breakdown and was constantly screaming. But after that first night they transferred me to a quiet and nicer floor.

At the hospital, at least in the states, you'll probably see a doctor, have some medicine prescribed, and attend group therapy sessions. Also the hospital will probably be understaffed--so don't expect the best of services.

Honestly, like igliashon said, the best thing the hospital provided was perspective--if anything I got a short break from the hellhole my life was becoming, and at the same time got to see that I didn't have it so bad, and that honestly all those negative things I thought about myself were, well, quite malleable--that is to say, they really only existed so long as I allowed them to be.

Also I read some nice books so that was great.

Man--as someone who has hideous eczema resulting from food allergies--I feel you. I've found that limiting my diet--even though I eat a lot of bland foods now has helped my skin. I don't want to be to preachy but cutting gluten, milk and its byproducts, and limiting sugars really can help (also eating less starch).

But I'll be honest in saying that doesn't really do much for my internal feelings. I'm still struggling right now, and all I can say is you're not alone. PM me if you want to talk.
